facts.statement: Crossvallia is an extinct genus of penguins.
facts.quote: Crossvallia is an extinct genus of penguins.

facts.statement: The genus Crossvallia includes two species: C. unienwillia and ?C. waiparensis.
facts.quote: It includes two species, C. unienwillia and ?C. waiparensis.

facts.statement: Anatomical evidence suggests that Crossvallia is closely related to the subfamily Anthropornithinae.
facts.quote: Their anatomy suggests that the genus is closely related to the Anthropornithinae.

facts.statement: Crossvallia belongs to the order Sphenisciformes and the family Spheniscidae.
facts.quote: Order Sphenisciformes Family Spheniscidae Genus Crossvallia

facts.statement: The species C. unienwillia was the first described in the genus, named after the Late Paleocene Cross Valley Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctica.
facts.quote: C. unienwillia was the first of the genus to be described, whose remains were recovered from and named after the Late Paleocene Cross Valley Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctica.

facts.statement: The species C. waiparensis was described in August 2019 based on leg bone fossils found in Waipara, New Zealand.
facts.quote: In August 2019, a new species of Crossvallia, C. waiparensis, was described based on leg bone fossils from Waipara, New Zealand.

facts.statement: The fossils of C. waiparensis were discovered in 2019 by amateur paleontologist Leigh Love.
facts.quote: The fossils were discovered in 2019 by amateur palaeontologist Leigh Love.

facts.statement: The species C. unienwillia measured approximately 140 cm in length.
C. waiparensis was significantly larger than the largest living penguin species, the Emperor penguin, which reaches about 121.9 cm and weighs up to 36 kg.
facts.quote: This is significantly large, considering the largest extant penguin species, the Emperor penguin, can be roughly around 121.9 cm, and weigh up to almost 36 kg.

facts.statement: Crossvallia is thought to have lived during the final stages of the Cretaceous and the Paleocene, between 66 and 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is thought to have lived in the final of Cretaceous and Paleocene 66–56 million years ago

facts.statement: The time range for Crossvallia is from the Selandian to the Thanetian stages, spanning 61.66 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Thanetian (61.66 to 56 million years ago)
